params.body:
## Why

The findings of a project live in its repository (`docs/bedrijfsregels/bevindingen/`, one file each, tied to the rules they contradict). That is the right place for the truth, but it is a poor place to triage: nobody assigns a markdown file, and a person who wants to see what is still open has to open the repository.

The plan (Shane, 19 September 2026) is to mirror open findings as GitHub issues: the file stays the source, the issue is the workbench, and the pull request that fixes it closes the issue and writes its number back into the file. A session may already push a branch and open a pull request through the gateway; opening the issue was the missing verb, and doing it with a personal token from a laptop is exactly what this gateway exists to prevent.

## What

- `issue.open` on `owner/repo`: `title` required; `body`, `labels` (at most ten short words) and `finding` (the path of the file it mirrors) optional.
- The GitHub adapter posts it and returns the number and the url, like `pull.open` does.
- The body carries the evidence footer, so a mirrored finding is distinguishable from an issue a person wrote.
- A new parameter type `[]string` in the schema: every element a word, the list bounded, because a parameter that can grow without end is a parameter nobody reads.

## Tests

`TestIssueOpenSchema` (a complete issue passes, no title is refused, a label that is not a word is refused, eleven labels are refused) plus the existing suites: `go test ./...` green, `gofmt` clean.

## After this

The kind also has to stand in the grant (`App\Control\Workbench` in elixir) and in `Capability::WORKBENCH_KINDS` (portal); the gateway demands both. Then a release and `rehearse.sh upgrade`.
params.title: issue.open: the gateway may mirror a finding as a GitHub issue
